label: Early-sequence input of u/e/v/n/c/3 (first three original positions)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase, at the first few positions (t=0..3 hold ~99% of mass; nothing past t=4). The input token matters most: u, e, v, n, c and 3 each have ~4x lift, and at t=0 the unit fires on exactly these six tokens with precision 1.0. At t=1 it is ~88% precise on these tokens, but it also fires on other tokens when the first token was one of the six (e.g. v 1, v g). At t=2 the token set alone is only ~35% precise, so the rest depends on history. The largest activations are at t=1-2 on u/e. It rarely fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase (~1% of mass), and it fires much less on repeated tokens (in_first=0). Predicate t<=2 & token in {u,e,v,n,c,3} reaches dev F1 0.71 and mass recall 0.78. Adding t==1 with prev_tok in the set raises mass recall to 0.85 but lowers precision.
